title: Quantized heat flow in moiré chern bands of bilayer graphene
authors: Santanu Samai, Debangan Sarkar, Abhijit Halder, T. Taniguchi, K. Watanabe, Subroto Mukerjee, Saurabh Kumar Srivastav, Anindya Das
abstract: When electrons are subjected simultaneously to a magnetic field and a periodic potential, they form the fractal Hofstadter spectrum, whose topological gaps host quantum Hall and Chern insulating states with distinct Chern numbers. While electrical transport has established the topology of these states, whether their heat transport is likewise universal has remained unexplored. Here, we measure the thermal conductance of quantum Hall, Chern insulator, and interaction-driven symmetry-broken Chern insulator states in a bilayer graphene-hexagonal boron nitride moiré superlattice with a moirè wavelength of $\sim$14 nm using Johnson-noise thermometry. We find that the thermal conductance ($G_Q$) is quantized in units of the thermal conductance quantum ($G_Q = tκ_0T$) and is determined solely by the Chern number ($t$), independent of the microscopic origin of the topological state. By directly revealing universal topological heat transport in Hofstadter bands, our work establishes thermal conductance as a stringent probe of moiré topological matter and provides a route to investigating more exotic phases, including fractional Chern insulators.
summary: The researchers measured the thermal conductance of topologically non-trivial states (like Chern insulators) in moiré graphene superlattices using advanced noise thermometry. They found that this heat flow is quantized based only on the system's topological Chern number, establishing thermal conductance as a universal diagnostic tool for moiré topology.
main_problem: To determine if heat transport in topological states (Quantum Hall, Chern Insulator) realized in moiré superlattices is universal, mirroring the established quantization of electrical transport.
main_result: The thermal conductance ($G_Q$) was found to be quantized in units determined solely by the Chern number ($t$), confirming universal topological heat transport.
method: Thermal conductance was measured using highly sensitive Johnson-noise thermometry, analyzing excess thermal noise and dissipated power as a function of source current.
model_or_system: The study uses bilayer graphene on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) moiré superlattices, which create Hofstadter spectra hosting various topological states parameterized by Chern numbers ($t$).
key_observables: Thermal conductance ($G_Q$), quantized values relative to the thermal quantum ($\kappa_0 T$), and electron temperature ($T_M$) derived from noise measurements.
important_parameters: Moiré wavelength ($\sim 14 	ext{ nm}$), magnetic field ($B_\perp$), Chern number ($t$), and the heat Coulomb blockade (HCB) effect.
main_assumptions: The quantization is assumed to be robust across different microscopic origins of topological states, though deviations at high $|t|$ are attributed to HCB or measurement limits.
figures_summary: Figures show device schematics, electrical transport measurements identifying QH/CI states, and thermal conductance plots confirming quantized plateaus for various Chern numbers.
paper_structure: The work progresses by first establishing the physical platform (BLG/hBN moiré superlattice) and characterizing topological states via electrical transport. It then details the advanced noise thermometry technique to measure $G_Q$, culminating in the demonstration of universal quantization across different topological regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct, measurable signature—quantized heat flow—that serves as a stringent probe for understanding and verifying exotic topological phases predicted in moiré materials, bridging electrical and thermal transport physics.
